variants.name: Transformed cultural allusion
variants.instruction: Rate how far a recognizable cultural artifact (a song, film, TV show, book, myth, advertisement, or named fictional character) is actively repurposed into the machinery of this joke. Apply the ladder in order and stop at the first rung that fits. 10 = a specific artifact is rebuilt: its plot, lyric, catchphrase, or character logic is bent to a new end and the punch is the bend itself. 8 = the artifact is genuinely reworked but the rework is small, a single altered word or line. 5 = the artifact supplies the joke's frame or setting and the joke could not run in a neutral setting, yet nothing about the artifact is altered. 3 = the artifact is present only as a familiar label attached to an otherwise self-contained gag; deleting the name and using a generic noun would cost recognition but not the mechanism. 1 = the artifact is quoted or name-dropped as pure decoration. 0 = the item contains no recognizable song, film, text, or character at all. Note that a bare name-drop is 1 and an item with no allusion whatsoever is 0; do not collapse these two cases together.
variants.rationale: Attacks the 85.2% pile at 0 by splitting the two very different populations the old rule sent to the same floor: items with no allusion at all, and items whose allusion is merely quoted. It also opens rungs 3, 5 and 8 for partial repurposing, which the old 10-or-0 wording had nowhere to put.

variants.name: Transformed cultural allusion
variants.instruction: Score the transformation of cultural allusion as the product of two graded judgments about this text. First, PRESENCE: how much recognizable cultural material is in the item, from 0 (none) through 1 (a passing brand or title) to 2 (a specific work, character, lyric or scene is invoked in detail). Second, WORK DONE: how much that material is altered or turned to a new purpose, from 0 (untouched, quoted or listed) through 1 (lightly twisted, a substituted word, a character behaving slightly off-model) to 2 (thoroughly repurposed; the original's own logic is the engine of the punch). Multiply and rescale: 0 stays 0, 1 becomes 3, 2 becomes 5, 3 becomes 7, 4 becomes 10. A 10 is an item where a specific well-known work is fully turned into new comic machinery; a 0 is an item with no recognizable cultural material to transform. Report only the final rescaled number.
variants.rationale: The old instruction fused recognizability and transformation into one all-or-nothing test, so anything short of full repurposing fell to 0. Decomposing into two three-point factors forces intermediate products (3, 5, 7) for the very common half-transformed and merely-invoked cases.

variants.name: Transformed cultural allusion
variants.instruction: Judge only this: if you replaced the referenced song, film, text or character with an invented equivalent that nobody recognizes, how much of the joke would break? Score 10 when the joke dies completely because the punch turns on a particular known detail of that artifact, and the item has visibly reshaped that detail rather than reciting it. Score 8 when the joke still limps but loses its point, because a real property of the artifact is being played with. Score 5 when the joke survives but reads as generic, because the artifact supplies flavour, setting or a familiar voice and nothing more. Score 2 when nothing at all changes except a lost flicker of recognition, which is the case for a pure name-drop or a quoted line. Score 0 when there is no cultural artifact in the item to substitute. Do not reward how famous the reference is or how many are present; a single obscure work fully repurposed outranks a crowd of famous names left untouched.
variants.rationale: Replaces the binary repurposed-versus-quoted gate with a substitution test whose answer is naturally continuous, and pins the empty case at 0 separately from the name-drop case at 2 so the huge modal bin splits.

variants.name: Teller as butt, with the admission doing comic work
variants.instruction: Score in two steps and average, rounding to the nearest whole number. STEP ONE, exposure: how unflattering is what the narrator reveals about their own habits, taste, competence, body, or character? 0 = the narrator is absent or reveals nothing about themselves, 5 = a mild or socially safe admission, 10 = a genuinely embarrassing or damaging confession. STEP TWO, comic load: how much of the laugh depends on that self-exposure? 0 = none, the joke works identically with a third person in the narrator's place, 5 = the self-exposure adds colour or a final sting to a joke that already worked, 10 = the confession is the punch; remove it and there is no joke. Average the two. A 10 is a narrator whose damaging admission is itself the payoff; a 0 is an item with no self-reference at all. An item where the narrator appears but is not the butt lands near 2 or 3, not at 0.
variants.rationale: The old wording was a conjunction (turns it on themselves AND the admission is the payoff), which the judge treated as a single pass-or-fail gate, dumping 81% at 0 and most of the rest at 10. Splitting the conjunction into two independently graded factors and averaging creates the missing middle and gives first-person-but-not-butt items a defined non-zero home.

variants.name: Teller as butt, with the admission doing comic work
variants.instruction: Score how far the teller is the target of their own joke, with the admission doing the comic work. Use these anchors. 10 = the speaker confesses something unflattering about their own habits, taste, or competence and that confession is the funniest element present. 8 = the speaker is clearly the butt and the admission carries most of the laugh, though a second gag shares the load. 6 = the speaker is the butt, but the humour comes mainly from a pun or situation and the self-indictment is the delivery vehicle. 4 = the speaker is implicated only by implication, for example a first-person narrator whose behaviour looks foolish but who never admits it. 2 = the narrator is present in the text but the joke's target is someone or something else. 1 = self-reference is used purely to pre-excuse weak material, or as a detachable apology. 0 = no first-person or self-referential material anywhere in the item. Choose the highest anchor the text fully satisfies.
variants.rationale: Attacks the 0-modal bin by naming, as separate rungs, the frequent cases the old text had no slot for: narrator present but not the butt, narrator implicitly foolish, and self-mockery riding on a pun. It also demotes the hedge case to 1 so that it stops sharing the floor with genuine absence of self-reference.

variants.name: Teller as butt, with the admission doing comic work
variants.instruction: Estimate the percentage of this joke's comic energy that comes from the narrator making themselves look bad, and convert directly to a 0-10 score (90-100% is 10, about half is 5, about a fifth is 2, none is 0). To do this, first check whether the text uses I, me, my, we, or an explicit stand-in for the teller; if it does not, score 0 and stop. If it does, ask what the reader is invited to laugh at. Score 10 when the answer is unambiguously the teller's own failing, taste, or incompetence, freely admitted. Score 5 when the reader laughs partly at the teller and partly at something external such as a wordplay or a third party. Score 2 when the teller is merely the camera, narrating a joke that lands on someone else. Score 1 when the self-reference exists only to apologize for or excuse the joke. Judge the text as written and do not speculate about the real person who typed it.
variants.rationale: Converts the pass-or-fail payoff test into a proportion, which is intrinsically continuous, and gives the very common first-person-narrator-as-camera case an explicit score of 2 instead of letting it fall into the 0 pile.

variants.name: Surprise from withholding the expected punchline
variants.instruction: Score how much this text builds an obvious expected punchline and then declines to deliver it, so that the refusal is itself the joke. Grade two things and average. EXPECTATION: how strongly is a specific next line signalled? 0 = nothing in particular is set up, 5 = a general comic shape is signalled without a specific line, 10 = the reader can all but recite the line that is coming. DENIAL: what actually arrives? 0 = exactly the expected line, delivered straight, 3 = a normal but different punchline, 5 = a deflating, mundane or literal answer where a joke was due, 8 = an answer that pointedly gestures at the withheld line without saying it, 10 = the text stops, refuses, or explicitly declines to complete the setup, and that stopping is clearly the intended payoff. Average and round. 10 means the expected line is loudly implied and pointedly withheld; 0 means nothing was set up and nothing was withheld.
variants.rationale: The 77% floor came from a single gate (was a punchline withheld, yes or no). Grading setup strength and denial type separately, then averaging, produces mid-range scores for the many items that subvert an expectation partially rather than refusing outright.

variants.name: Surprise from withholding the expected punchline
variants.instruction: Rate the presence of withheld-punchline surprise using this ladder; pick the highest rung the text fully meets. 10 = the setup makes one specific line inevitable, the text refuses to say it, and the refusal is the entire payoff. 8 = the expected line is withheld and replaced by a flat, literal or irrelevant statement whose flatness is clearly deliberate. 6 = a different punchline arrives that comments on the expected one, for instance by pointing at it or side-stepping it. 4 = a different punchline arrives that is simply a swerve, with no reference to what was expected. 2 = the delivered punchline is the expected kind but a weaker or milder version of it. 0 = the setup leads to its natural punchline and it is delivered normally, or there is no clear setup at all. Do not confuse a joke you personally found unsurprising with a joke that withholds; withholding requires that the text itself made a particular line expected.
variants.rationale: Names the intermediate species the old wording ignored, especially the swerve to a different punchline (rung 4) and the mild version (rung 2), which the judge previously had to force to either 0 or 10.

variants.name: Surprise from withholding the expected punchline
variants.instruction: Ask two questions in order. First: while reading, did you form a concrete guess at the final line before reaching it? If not, the item cannot withhold anything, so score 0 or 1 depending on whether any anticipation at all was created. If yes, second: how far is what actually arrived from your guess, and does the gap read as intentional? Score 10 when your guess never appears and its absence is conspicuous, which is the whole point of the item. Score 7 when your guess is dodged by something plainly anticlimactic. Score 5 when your guess is replaced by an unrelated line of equal ambition. Score 3 when your guess is partially delivered, hedged, or arrives in weakened form. Score 0 when your guess is exactly what arrived. Note explicitly that most jokes in this corpus deliver a normal punchline and therefore belong at 0-1, but jokes that swerve belong in the middle, not at the floor.
variants.rationale: Removes the escape hatch of treating anything that is not a pure refusal as punchline-delivered-normally, and states outright where the common swerve case sits, so the mass at 0 is redistributed into 3-7.

variants.name: Wordplay with homophone or near-homophone pivot
variants.instruction: Score how much the humour depends on a word or phrase sounding like a different word or phrase with another meaning. Grade the phonetic distance and the load together. 10 = one exact homophone or perfect sound-alike carries the whole joke; hear it wrong and there is no joke. 8 = an exact sound-alike carries the punch, but a second mechanism such as a situation or an absurd image also contributes. 6 = a near-homophone that needs a slight stretch of pronunciation, accent, or elision carries the punch. 4 = the pun is on one word with two meanings and identical spelling and sound, so nothing has to be re-heard, only re-read. 2 = a faint sound echo, alliteration, rhyme, or spoonerism is present and adds flavour but the joke stands without it. 0 = no phonetic play of any kind. Note that same-spelling double meaning belongs at 4, not at 10 and not at 0.
variants.rationale: The histogram is almost purely 0 or 10 because the old wording admitted only a whole-joke exact homophone or nothing. Naming near-homophones, polysemy without sound change, and decorative sound echoes as separate rungs gives the judge somewhere to put the large intermediate population.

variants.name: Wordplay with homophone or near-homophone pivot
variants.instruction: Perform a read-aloud test and score the result. Read the item aloud in your head. Score 10 when a spoken word is genuinely ambiguous between two meanings and the joke resolves only when the reader hears the second one; the pivot word can be pointed to. Score 7 when the two words differ by one sound or one syllable boundary, so the pivot needs a small push to work. Score 5 when the joke needs the sound but the second meaning is signalled in the spelling too, so the reader gets it by eye and the ear only confirms. Score 3 when the sound similarity is a garnish sitting beside the real mechanism, or the item leans on rhyme rather than on ambiguity. Score 0 when nothing in the item changes meaning when heard rather than read. Judge only the phonetic mechanism, not whether the pun is good, groan-worthy, or original.
variants.rationale: Attacks the near-binary distribution by making the graded quantity phonetic distance and channel (ear versus eye), which varies continuously across items, rather than the binary is-there-a-homophone question.

variants.name: Wordplay with homophone or near-homophone pivot
variants.instruction: Score the proportion of the joke's mechanism that rests on sound. Ask what would remain if the reader were unable to hear the words and could only see them. Score 10 when nothing remains: the item is a bare homophone pivot with no other content. Score 8 when the item has a small amount of independent setup or imagery, but the pivot is still an exact sound-alike. Score 6 when a sound-alike pivot exists but part of the humour also comes from the picture or situation it creates. Score 4 when the item plays on a word with more than one sense and the senses are spelled the same, so no listening is required. Score 2 when there is only assonance, rhyme, a name that sounds vaguely like something, or a stretched resemblance that has to be pointed out. Score 0 when the item's humour survives entirely intact without any sound relationship. Assign the score even when the phonetic play is bad or forced; badness belongs at the same rung as goodness.
variants.rationale: Removes the implicit quality filter (a strained resemblance previously read as no phonetic ambiguity, sending it to 0) and reframes the target as a proportion, which produces intermediate values for partial phonetic dependence.

variants.name: No self-explanation or apology attached to the pun
variants.instruction: Score how far the item trusts the reader by letting its final beat land without commentary. Treat the last line that produces the humour as the punch, whether or not it is a pun; every item has one, so there is no unscorable case. Count the assists present in the text: (a) a pre-announcement that a joke or pun is coming, (b) naming the device, for example calling it a pun, a dad joke, or wordplay, (c) an apology or self-deprecating tag such as an admission that the joke is bad or an announcement of leaving, (d) an explanation after the punch of why it works, (e) typed laughter, a rimshot, an emoji, or a groan noise, (f) restating the punch in plainer words. Score 10 with zero assists present and nothing at all after the punch. Score 8 when a short unrelated flourish follows that adds its own content but does not comment on the joke. Score 6 when one mild assist of type (e) alone is present. Score 4 with one assist of types (a), (b), or (c). Score 2 with two or more assists, or with any assist of types (d) or (f). Score 0 when the text both explains the mechanism and apologizes for it.
variants.rationale: 96.8% sat at 10 because the old rule asked one question (does anything follow?) that almost all items pass, and its pun framing produced NA for non-pun items. Enumerating six distinct assist types and letting the count drive the score creates a real spread, and defining the punch for any item eliminates the NA escape hatch.

variants.name: No self-explanation or apology attached to the pun
variants.instruction: Judge whether this item lets its joke land unassisted, on a scale where the ceiling is genuinely hard to reach. 10 = the text ends on the beat that produces the humour, the very last word is load-bearing, and there is no signposting anywhere, including at the start. 9 = clean but with a small orienting phrase before the setup that hints a joke is coming. 7 = a short tag follows the punch that is itself a further joke rather than a comment on the joke. 5 = a brief flourish, aside, or emoticon follows that neither explains nor apologizes but does deflate the ending. 3 = the text signals in advance that a pun or joke is arriving, or ends by naming the device used. 1 = the text explains the joke, spells out the double meaning, or repeats the punch in clearer language. 0 = the text apologizes for the joke's quality or performs an exit line about how bad it was. If the item contains no wordplay, apply exactly the same rules to whatever its final comic beat is.
variants.rationale: Attacks the ceiling pile by pulling apart the many things that count as clean: an item ending exactly on its load-bearing word is distinguished from one with a harmless trailing flourish or an opening announcement, so the top bin is no longer a catch-all.

variants.name: No self-explanation or apology attached to the pun
variants.instruction: Measure the ratio of joke to commentary about the joke. Identify the moment the humour fires. Then ask how many words in the item exist to manage the reader's reaction to it rather than to build or deliver the joke, counting both before and after that moment. Score 10 when that count is zero. Score 8 when it is one or two words, for instance a trailing ellipsis or a single interjection. Score 6 when a short clause of reaction management is present but the joke itself is untouched by it. Score 4 when a whole sentence is devoted to framing, announcing, or reacting to the joke. Score 2 when the commentary explains how the joke works. Score 0 when the commentary both explains and disowns the joke, or when there is more commentary than joke. Apply this to every item, including items with no pun; a story or observation with no wordplay is scored on the same ratio.
variants.rationale: Replaces a yes-or-no test with a countable quantity that varies item to item, and closes the NA route by stating that pun-free items are scored identically, which should shrink both the 3.3% NA rate and the 96.8% ceiling bin.

variants.name: Insider knowledge gate with a self-verifying payoff
variants.instruction: Score in two independent parts and average, rounding to the nearest whole number. PART ONE, gate height: how much specific technical, scientific, mathematical, or subcultural knowledge must a reader already hold to decode this item? 0 = none, 3 = a fact taught in general schooling or common in popular culture, 6 = a fact familiar to anyone with a hobbyist interest in the field, 10 = a fact only a practitioner or serious enthusiast would hold. PART TWO, enactment: does the payoff perform the invoked property or merely mention it? 0 = the domain word is scenery, 3 = the domain fact is stated and the joke comments on it, 6 = the joke's structure partly mirrors the fact, 10 = the punch is a live demonstration of the very property invoked, such as an item about an unreliable protocol that may not arrive, or a quantity that is literally the root of another. Average the two parts. 10 means a practitioner-level gate whose punch enacts the fact; 0 means no specialist knowledge is invoked at all.
variants.rationale: The old text joined a knowledge requirement and an enactment requirement with AND, and the judge failed the whole item when either half was weak, producing 77.6% zeros. Scoring the two halves separately and averaging lets a strong gate with a weak enactment, and vice versa, land in the middle.

variants.name: Insider knowledge gate with a self-verifying payoff
variants.instruction: Rate this item on an insider-knowledge gate whose payoff verifies itself, using the highest matching rung. 10 = decoding demands real domain knowledge and the punchline enacts the exact property invoked. 8 = decoding demands real domain knowledge and the punch depends precisely on that fact, though it describes rather than enacts it. 6 = the joke needs a specialist fact, but a reader without it could still infer the shape of the gag from context. 5 = domain vocabulary appears and the gag reduces to a generic pun any reader could get. 3 = the item is set in a specialist world such as a lab, a server room, or a clinic, and uses its vocabulary as colour while the joke itself is general. 1 = a single technical word appears with no bearing on the mechanism. 0 = no specialist knowledge is needed or invoked at any point. Judge the load the knowledge carries, not how difficult the field is or whether you find the item clever.
variants.rationale: Fills in the region between the old 5 anchor and the old 0 by naming the very common specialist-setting and lone-jargon-word cases, which previously had no home and defaulted to the zero pile.

variants.name: Insider knowledge gate with a self-verifying payoff
variants.instruction: Run a two-reader thought experiment. Reader A knows nothing beyond general culture; Reader B is an expert in whatever field the item touches. Score 10 when Reader A gets nothing whatsoever and Reader B gets a punch that acts out the property it names, so the form of the joke is itself an instance of the fact. Score 8 when Reader A gets nothing and Reader B gets a punch that turns on the fact without acting it out. Score 6 when Reader A gets a partial or lesser joke and Reader B gets a distinctly better one. Score 4 when both readers get the same joke but Reader B also recognizes the terminology as accurate. Score 2 when the field is only a costume and Reader B gains nothing beyond familiarity. Score 0 when there is no field to be expert in. Score accuracy of the invoked fact only insofar as an error would stop Reader B from getting the joke; do not deduct for the field being an easy one.
variants.rationale: Converts the two-part conjunction into a comparison between two readers, which yields a naturally graded gap, and gives the frequent costume-only and accurate-terminology cases explicit low-but-nonzero anchors so they leave the modal bin.

variants.name: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops
variants.instruction: List every shared reference the item invokes: named people, products, brands, platforms, news events, places, and ordinary shared situations such as commuting or a waiting room. For each one, name out loud the specific property of that referent the punch exploits, then test whether swapping it for a different referent of the same category would break the joke. Score by the fraction of references that pass both checks. 10 = every reference passes; you can state the exploited property for each and each substitution breaks the joke. 8 = the main reference passes and a secondary one is decorative. 5 = roughly half pass, or the single reference passes only partly, its general category mattering while its particular identity does not. 3 = one reference does mild work while the rest are recognition bait. 0 = no reference does any work; all are interchangeable. If you cannot state the specific exploited property in words, that reference has failed. An item built on an ordinary shared situation can reach 10, but only if you can name the precise feature of that situation the punch turns on; if the situation is merely a setting, score 3 or below. Do not reward how many references appear, how current they are, or how fashionable the vocabulary is, and do not judge whether the item is funny.
variants.rationale: 81.5% sat at 10 because the ordinary-shared-experience clause let almost any everyday setup qualify as load-bearing by default. Requiring the exploited property to be named explicitly, and defaulting unnamed cases to 3 or below, removes that escape hatch, while the fraction-passing rule creates genuine intermediate scores.

variants.name: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops
variants.instruction: Judge only how hard the item's references work, on this ladder. 10 = the punch turns on a particular and true property of a specific referent, and no other referent in the same category could be substituted without destroying the joke. 8 = substitution would badly damage the joke but a small set of close cousins would still work. 6 = the referent's broad type matters but its identity does not; any doctor, any airline, any social platform would serve. 4 = the referent supplies a recognizable scene the joke needs, without any property of it being exploited. 2 = the referent is present for recognition or flavour and the punch would survive its removal. 0 = every reference is fully interchangeable, or the item is a bare abstract gag with nothing shared to exploit. A dense cluster of very recognisable names, none of them exploited, scores 0 regardless of how topical they are. Do not judge whether the item is funny; judge only whether its references do work.
variants.rationale: Attacks the ceiling pile by inserting the type-matters-but-identity-does-not rung at 6 and the scene-supplying rung at 4, which is where a large share of everyday-situation jokes actually belong and where the old binary phrasing had no slot.

variants.name: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops
variants.instruction: Apply a written substitution test and grade the damage on a continuum. Pick the single reference the punch most depends on. Replace it with a plausible different member of the same category and reread the item. Score 10 if the joke is now nonsense, because the punch relied on a fact true of that referent alone. Score 7 if the joke still parses but has clearly lost its point. Score 5 if the joke is equally good with the substitute, but the category itself was necessary. Score 3 if the joke is unchanged and the reference was setting or scenery. Score 0 if the reference could be deleted entirely without loss, or if the item consists of names presented for recognition alone. For items with no proper nouns, treat the ordinary shared situation as the reference and run the same substitution: swap the commute for a queue, the waiting room for a bus stop, and grade the damage identically. Ignore reference count, topicality, and fashionableness, and do not score funniness.
variants.rationale: Forces the same concrete damage test on reference-free everyday items instead of granting them a default pass, which is what drove both the 10-heavy histogram and the 5.6% NA rate, and produces a graded answer since damage varies by item.

variants.name: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land
variants.instruction: Judge whether the setup supplies exactly what the punch needs, and grade the number and severity of resolution defects rather than answering yes or no. Read to the final line and ask what it depends on: every premise, referent, pronoun antecedent, and detail. Then count defects of two kinds, MISSING (something the punch needs never arrived, or arrived too late) and SPOILED (something the punch was to reveal was already given away). Score 10 for zero defects: everything needed is present, correctly ordered, and nothing is pre-revealed. Score 8 for one trivial defect a reader repairs without noticing, such as a loose pronoun with only one plausible antecedent. Score 6 for one real defect that costs a beat of rereading. Score 4 for one defect that forces the reader to guess at the intended meaning. Score 2 for two or more real defects, or for a punch that half-resolves. Score 0 when the mechanism cannot resolve at all: the punch relies on something never supplied, the text stops before the mechanism completes, or the payload was fully given away in the setup. A misspelt, lowercase, unpunctuated, run-on item scores 10 if its logical scaffolding is intact. Do not score spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, layout, markup artifacts, or prose polish; do not score funniness.
variants.rationale: The histogram is perfectly binary, 0 or 10, because the old wording posed one question with a yes-or-no answer. Making the score a function of defect count and defect severity gives the judge an explicit reason to use 2, 4, 6 and 8.

variants.name: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land
variants.instruction: Score how completely the setup arms the punch, using the amount of repair work the reader must do. 10 = zero repair; on a first pass the final line lands with every premise already in hand and nothing pre-revealed. 9 = a single reread of one phrase is enough. 7 = the reader must supply one small piece of ordinary world knowledge that the text assumed but did not state, and would plainly have. 5 = the reader must guess at one referent or connective, and a reasonable reader could guess wrong. 3 = a needed premise is genuinely absent and only a charitable reader reconstructs the intended joke. 1 = the punch is partly spoiled by the setup, so something lands but weakly. 0 = the mechanism cannot resolve: a pronoun points at nothing, the text stops early, or the reveal was already delivered. Judge logic and information order only. Ignore spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, run-ons and markup; an unfunny joke whose logic is fully supplied scores 10.
variants.rationale: Recasts a binary structural check as a graded quantity of reader repair effort, and explicitly names the partial-spoiler and assumed-world-knowledge cases, which the old text forced into one of the two extremes.

variants.name: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land
variants.instruction: Score the setup on three checks worth up to 4, 3 and 3 points respectively; sum them. CHECK ONE, referents, up to 4 points: award 4 if every pronoun, name and definite noun phrase the punch depends on has a clear antecedent in the text, 2 if one is ambiguous but recoverable, 0 if one points at nothing. CHECK TWO, completeness, up to 3 points: award 3 if every fact the punch turns on has been supplied before it is needed, 1 or 2 if a fact is supplied late or only implied, 0 if it is never supplied. CHECK THREE, withholding, up to 3 points: award 3 if the thing the punch reveals is genuinely still hidden at the moment the punch arrives, 1 or 2 if it was partly telegraphed, 0 if it was already stated outright. A total of 10 means a fully armed, correctly ordered setup; a total of 0 means the mechanism cannot resolve at all. Score logical scaffolding only: ignore spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, run-ons, layout and markup, and ignore whether the item is funny.
variants.rationale: Decomposing the single gate into three separately scored components makes intermediate totals arithmetically unavoidable, directly breaking the 0-or-10 collapse without changing what the criterion is about.

variants.name: Economy and timing of information release before the punch
variants.instruction: Score economy and timing as two separate five-point judgments and add them. ECONOMY, 0 to 5: 5 = nothing could be deleted without breaking the mechanism, 4 = one phrase is spare, 3 = one sentence is spare or one beat is stated twice, 2 = noticeable filler preamble or repetition, 1 = most of the text is padding, 0 = the item is mostly restatement. TIMING, 0 to 5: 5 = the word or phrase that flips the meaning sits at or very near the end, where it flips the most, and nothing follows it, 4 = the flip is near the end with a short harmless tail, 3 = the flip is followed by a sentence that adds a little, 2 = the turn is signposted in advance so the reader sees it coming, 1 = the flip sits mid-text and the ending restates it, 0 = the mechanism is explained after it fires. Add for a 0-10 total. A rambling narrative can still score 10 if each digression is a plant the ending uses. Do not reward conformity to any template, shortness for its own sake, speaker labels, or tidy layout, and do not judge whether the item is funny.
variants.rationale: 76% sat at 10 because the old text listed many conditions joined by and, and the judge treated satisfying the general spirit as a pass. Splitting into two additive five-point subscales forces graded credit for the very common case of a well-timed but slightly padded item, or a tight item with a trailing tail.

variants.name: Economy and timing of information release before the punch
variants.instruction: Apply a deletion test and a position test, then take the lower of the two resulting scores. DELETION TEST: try removing each sentence or clause in turn. Score 10 if no removal leaves the joke intact, 7 if one removal is harmless, 5 if two are, 3 if a third of the text can go, 0 if half or more can go. POSITION TEST: locate the exact word at which the meaning flips. Score 10 if it is in the final few words, 7 if it is in the final sentence but with words trailing after it, 5 if it is in the middle and the ending merely completes the sentence, 3 if the ending restates or explains it, 0 if the item announces its turn before making it. Report the lower score. A one-line item scores low if half of it is redundant; a long narrative scores high if every digression is a plant. Do not reward brevity, templates, speaker labels or layout, and do not judge funniness; a flat joke with perfect timing scores 10 and a hilarious one that explains itself afterwards scores low.
variants.rationale: Replaces holistic assent with two mechanical tests whose outputs are graded, and the take-the-lower rule prevents the judge from awarding a ceiling score to items that merely pass one of the two.

variants.name: Economy and timing of information release before the punch
variants.instruction: Estimate what fraction of the words before the final beat are doing real work, and where the decisive element sits, then score on this ladder. 10 = essentially every word earns its place and the flipping element lands last. 9 = one small redundancy or one word of tail, otherwise perfect. 8 = a short throat-clearing opening, otherwise tight and correctly timed. 6 = a workable but loose text, with a repeated beat or a paragraph that could be a sentence, still ending on the flip. 5 = well-shaped but the reader is told in advance what kind of turn is coming. 4 = the flipping element arrives before the ending and the ending restates it. 2 = substantial filler, or the same beat stated twice, or a clause of explanation after the punch. 0 = the item wastes the reader throughout, or explains its own mechanism after it fires. Assume that a genuinely flawless item is uncommon; reserve 10 for texts you could not trim by a single word. Do not reward templates, shortness, speaker labels or layout, and do not judge whether the item is funny.
variants.rationale: States explicitly that the ceiling is uncommon and supplies nearby rungs (9, 8, 6) for the near-clean items that were previously all rounded up to 10, which is the direct source of the modal share.

variants.name: Controlled anti-joke framing
variants.instruction: Score how deliberately the item sets up a conventional joke expectation and then makes banality, refusal, or withholding the actual payoff. Grade the setup and the payoff separately and average. SETUP, 0 to 10: how clearly does the item adopt a recognizable joke form, such as a walks-into-a-bar opening, a question-and-answer shape, a rule of three, or a familiar riddle stem? 0 = no joke form is invoked, 5 = a loose comic framing, 10 = an unmistakable template the reader knows how to complete. PAYOFF, 0 to 10: 0 = a normal punchline arrives, 3 = a weak or ordinary punchline arrives, 5 = a literal or mundane answer arrives which may or may not be intentional, 8 = a flatly banal answer arrives that is clearly played straight for effect, 10 = the expected payoff is refused outright and the refusal is unmistakably the joke. Average and round. Score 0 when neither a joke expectation nor a deliberate deflation is present, and score low rather than high when incompleteness looks accidental.
variants.rationale: The 76% floor came from a single deliberateness gate. Splitting the item into how strongly the template is invoked and how the payoff behaves, then averaging, produces mid-range scores for the many items that partially deflate.

variants.name: Controlled anti-joke framing
variants.instruction: Rate the controlled anti-joke framing on this ladder, choosing the highest rung the text fully meets. 10 = a conventional joke setup is followed by a deliberately banal, literal, or absent payoff, and the deliberateness is unmistakable because the setup's machinery is precisely built for it. 8 = a familiar setup is followed by a flatly ordinary statement whose flatness reads as intended. 6 = a familiar setup is followed by a mundane answer where intent is plausible but not certain. 4 = a familiar setup is followed by an ordinary punchline that is merely mild rather than deflating. 2 = a joke shape is present and the ending is incomplete or weak in a way that reads as accidental. 0 = there is no conventional joke expectation to defeat, or a normal punchline is delivered with full commitment. Judge intent from the text's own construction, not from how funny you find it; a well-built anti-joke and a badly built one are scored on control, not on quality.
variants.rationale: Attacks the zero pile by giving the accidental-looking and merely-mild cases explicit rungs at 2 and 4 rather than letting them share the floor with items that invoke no joke expectation at all.

variants.name: Controlled anti-joke framing
variants.instruction: Ask what the item does with the expectation it creates. Score 10 when it manufactures a strong expectation of a punchline and then pays it off with something pointedly ordinary, obvious, or with nothing at all, and the whole construction exists to produce that thud. Score 7 when the payoff is deflating but the item also carries a real gag alongside the deflation. Score 5 when the payoff is literal and unremarkable and you cannot tell whether the flatness is the point. Score 3 when the item merely under-delivers on a promise, as with a punchline that is present but limp. Score 1 when the text breaks off or fails to complete in a way that looks unintended rather than staged. Score 0 when no conventional joke expectation is created at all, or the expectation is met in the ordinary way. Note that the middle of this scale is where uncertain intent belongs; do not resolve uncertainty by defaulting to 0.
variants.rationale: Names the ambiguity resolution explicitly, since the old wording (score 0 when incompleteness appears accidental) invited the judge to dump every uncertain case at the floor, which is the likely source of the 76% modal share.

variants.name: Site-native self-reference that still executes a turn
variants.instruction: Score how far the item uses the culture of the posting forum itself as the machinery of its joke rather than as its subject. Community material means posting, reposting, karma, upvotes, comments, the front page, mods, or the sub as such, appearing in the text. 10 = community material sets up a genuine reversal, self-implication, or unexpected turn that would collapse if the community frame were removed. 8 = the community frame drives a real turn, but the turn would survive in weakened form elsewhere. 6 = community material is integral to the situation and produces a mild twist. 4 = community material is the joke's topic and it voices a familiar complaint or asserts membership, with no turn. 2 = insider vocabulary appears as decoration only. 0 = the item contains no community material at all. Do not score 5 as a default; every item receives a rung on this ladder, and the very common case of no community material belongs at 0. Judge only the text.
variants.rationale: 96.5% sat at exactly 5 because the old wording ordered the judge to score 5 and stop whenever community material was absent, which is most items. Removing that hatch and placing absence at 0, while grading the presence cases across 2 to 10, converts a degenerate constant into a real distribution.

variants.name: Site-native self-reference that still executes a turn
variants.instruction: Grade two things and average, rounding to the nearest whole number. AMOUNT of site-native material, 0 to 10: 0 = none, 3 = a single passing mention of posting, reposting, karma, comments, mods, or the sub, 6 = the item is set inside forum behaviour, 10 = the item is entirely about forum behaviour. TURN, 0 to 10: 0 = no turn; the item states a complaint, an observation, or a membership claim, 5 = a light reversal or ironic snap at the end, 10 = a genuine reversal or self-implication that collapses if the community frame is removed. Average the two. This means an item with no site-native material scores 0, an item that is pure community grumbling scores about 3, and an item whose community frame powers a real twist scores 8 to 10. Insider vocabulary on its own contributes to AMOUNT but nothing to TURN.
variants.rationale: Replaces the composite first-gate-then-score structure, which produced a constant 5 for the majority, with two graded factors and an average, so both the absence case and the complaint-without-turn case get distinct low scores instead of the same default.

variants.name: Site-native self-reference that still executes a turn
variants.instruction: Perform a frame-removal test. If the item mentions nothing about posting, reposting, karma, comments, mods, the front page, or the sub, score 0 and stop; absence of site-native material is the bottom of this scale, not the middle. Otherwise, mentally strip the community frame, rewriting posting as speaking and the sub as any room of people, and reread. Score 10 if the joke collapses entirely, because the reversal or self-implication depended on the frame. Score 7 if the joke survives but loses its bite. Score 5 if the joke is unchanged in force and the frame merely localized it. Score 3 if the item is a familiar complaint about the community, or an assertion of membership, with no turn to lose. Score 1 if only insider vocabulary is present, sprinkled onto an unrelated gag. Judge the text as written and do not speculate about who posted it or when.
variants.rationale: Keeps the composite concept intact but relocates the default: the escape hatch that assigned 5 to the overwhelming majority is replaced by an explicit 0 floor, and the surviving cases are graded by collapse damage, which varies continuously.

variants.name: Textual coherence as a genuine joke vs. fragment/spam
variants.instruction: Score how fully the text reads as a coherent, purposeful joke in fluent English. 10 = fully coherent and clearly intended as a joke; sentences parse, the structure is recognizable, and a reader would never mistake it for anything else. 8 = coherent and clearly a joke, with minor roughness such as a typo, a missing article, or slightly odd phrasing that never impedes comprehension. 6 = comprehensible and recognizably a joke, but awkward enough that a sentence must be reread, or with a mildly garbled clause. 4 = a joke is discernible but the text is substantially broken: mangled syntax, missing words, or apparent machine translation. 2 = only a fragment of joke-like material survives amid incoherence, or a joke shape is visible but the content does not resolve into anything. 1 = promotional or keyword-stuffed text with a thin joke veneer. 0 = incoherent, pure ad copy, spam, keyword-stuffing, or a fragment that does not cohere into any recognizable joke structure. Judge coherence and joke-shape only, not whether the joke is funny or original.
variants.rationale: 75.6% sat at 10 because the old rule was a two-way sort into coherent-joke or spam-fragment. Naming degrees of roughness at 8, 6 and 4 and separating thin-veneer promotional text at 1 from outright incoherence at 0 gives the judge places to put the large partially-rough population.

variants.name: Textual coherence as a genuine joke vs. fragment/spam
variants.instruction: Score two aspects and take the lower. FLUENCY: 10 = idiomatic, correctly built English throughout, 7 = minor errors that never slow the reader, 5 = errors that force one reread, 3 = frequently broken syntax, 0 = unreadable. JOKE-SHAPE: 10 = a complete comic structure, setup and payoff both present and purposeful, 7 = a complete structure with a slack or unclear component, 5 = recognizably intended as humour but structurally incomplete, 3 = a fragment with only a hint of comic intent, 0 = no comic structure at all, or the text is advertisement, spam, or keyword-stuffing. Report the lower of the two numbers. This means a beautifully written non-joke and a genuine joke written unreadably both score low, while only items that are both fluent and structurally complete reach the top. Do not judge whether the joke is funny, tasteful, or original.
variants.rationale: The old single question let any item that was broadly readable and broadly joke-shaped pass to 10. Requiring both dimensions and reporting the minimum forces the score down for the many items that are strong on one axis and mediocre on the other.

variants.name: Textual coherence as a genuine joke vs. fragment/spam
variants.instruction: Count the comprehension obstacles in this text and score accordingly. Obstacles include: a sentence that cannot be parsed on first reading, a missing or duplicated word that changes the sense, an unresolvable reference, an abrupt stop mid-thought, formatting or markup debris interleaved with the words, promotional or keyword-stuffed material, and an ending that does not deliver anything a reader would recognize as a payoff. Score 10 with no obstacles at all. Score 8 with one cosmetic obstacle that a reader repairs instantly. Score 6 with one genuine obstacle. Score 4 with two. Score 2 with three or more, or with any single obstacle that prevents the item from resolving into a joke. Score 0 when the text is incoherent throughout, is advertisement or spam, or is a bare fragment. Judge only comprehensibility and whether a joke is recognizably being attempted, never whether the attempt succeeds in being funny.
variants.rationale: Converts a binary sort into a defect count, which is naturally graded, and explicitly lists formatting debris and mid-thought stops so that borderline items stop being rounded up into the 10 bin.

variants.name: Long scaffolding erected for one terminal pun
variants.instruction: Score how far this item is long scaffolding erected for one terminal pun. Grade two factors and average. SCAFFOLD SIZE, 0 to 10: 0 = the setup is a single clause, 3 = one or two sentences, 6 = a short paragraph, list, or verse, 10 = several paragraphs or a full narrative. REVERSE-ENGINEERING, 0 to 10: 0 = the setup is genuinely interesting on its own terms and would survive without the ending, 3 = mostly independent with one clause bent toward the ending, 5 = a mixture, some material doing independent work and some visibly bent, 8 = nearly all the setup exists to make the final line possible, 10 = every clause is transparently chosen so that one final pun becomes grammatical, and the setup has no independent life at all. Average and round. A 10 is a long, wholly reverse-engineered edifice ending in a single pun; a 0 is a one-clause setup, or a setup that stands on its own. Reward the diagnosis of reverse-engineering, not length as such.
variants.rationale: The 76% zero pile came from an implicit conjunction of length and reverse-engineering, failed by any short item. Grading the two dimensions separately and averaging gives short-but-contrived and long-but-independent items real middle scores instead of the floor.

variants.name: Long scaffolding erected for one terminal pun
variants.instruction: Ask whether the setup was written forwards or backwards, and how much of it there is. Choose the highest rung that fits. 10 = paragraphs of narrative, list, or verse exist for no reason other than to make one final pun grammatical, and you can point at individual clauses that only exist to place a needed word. 8 = a substantial setup, most of which is visibly reverse-engineered, ending in one terminal pun. 6 = a moderate setup, clearly built toward a final pun, though parts of it are entertaining in themselves. 5 = a moderate setup, some of which does independent work, ending in a pun. 3 = a short setup ending in a pun, with no sign of contortion. 1 = the item ends in a pun but the setup is a single clause. 0 = the item has no terminal pun, or the setup is genuinely interesting on its own terms and the ending is not the reason it exists. Score construction, not length and not quality; a laboured masterpiece and a laboured groaner sit at the same rung.
variants.rationale: Names the frequent short-pun and moderately-built cases at rungs 1, 3 and 6, which the old wording pushed to 0 because they lacked paragraphs of scaffolding, and separates having no terminal pun (0) from having a small one (1).

variants.name: Long scaffolding erected for one terminal pun
variants.instruction: Estimate what proportion of the setup material exists solely to make the last line work, and convert to a score: about 100% is 10, about 80% is 8, about half is 5, about a quarter is 3, near zero is 0. To estimate it, take each sentence or clause of the setup and ask whether a writer who had not yet chosen the ending could plausibly have written it. Clauses that only a writer who already knew the punchline would produce, such as an oddly specific profession, an unmotivated foreign character, or a strained plural, count toward the proportion. Then apply one adjustment: if the setup is a single clause, cap the score at 2, because there is not enough scaffolding to speak of. Score 0 when the item ends in no pun at all, or when the setup would be worth reading with the ending removed. Do not reward or penalize length in itself, and do not judge whether the pun is any good.
variants.rationale: Makes the target an estimated proportion with a concrete detection heuristic, so the answer varies continuously, and replaces the hard length gate with a soft cap that still leaves short items nonzero rather than dumping them in the modal bin.

variants.name: Specialist-domain knowledge as the hinge
variants.instruction: Score how far the joke turns on a fact from a technical or specialist domain such as chemistry, mathematics, networking, physics, programming, biology, linguistics, law, medicine, or psychoanalysis, such that the reader must already hold that fact for the punchline to resolve. Grade two factors and average. SPECIALISM, 0 to 10: 0 = no domain content, 3 = a fact from general schooling such as basic arithmetic or the periodic table's most famous entries, 6 = a fact a hobbyist or undergraduate would hold, 10 = a fact requiring genuine practitioner familiarity. LOAD, 0 to 10: 0 = the domain word is scenery, 3 = the fact adds flavour to a joke that works without it, 5 = a technical veneer over a joke that works anyway, 8 = the fact is needed, though context hints at the answer, 10 = a reader without the fact gets nothing at all. Average and round. Score the load the domain fact carries, not how hard the domain is on its own.
variants.rationale: 88.6% sat at 0 because the old text required a genuine, accurately deployed domain fact whose absence leaves the reader with nothing, all at once. Splitting specialism from load and averaging lets the abundant middle, general-knowledge science and flavour-only jargon, occupy real intermediate scores.

variants.name: Specialist-domain knowledge as the hinge
variants.instruction: Choose the highest rung this item fully meets. 10 = the hinge is a genuine specialist fact, deployed accurately, and a reader without that fact gets nothing at all. 8 = a specialist fact is the hinge and is accurate, but a reader lacking it could sense that a joke happened. 7 = the hinge is a fact from a technical domain that is nonetheless widely known outside it, such as a famous constant or a well-known element. 5 = a technical veneer over a joke that works anyway. 4 = specialist vocabulary supplies the setting and a little of the flavour, while the mechanism is general. 2 = a single technical word appears with no role in the mechanism. 0 = no specialist content of any kind. Judge the load the domain fact carries, not how hard the domain is; do not deduct for the domain being an easy one, and do not add for it being obscure if the fact carries no load.
variants.rationale: Adds the widely-known-technical-fact rung at 7 and the setting-only rung at 4, the two populations most likely to have been swept into the zero pile by the old requirement that a reader without the fact must get nothing.

variants.name: Specialist-domain knowledge as the hinge
variants.instruction: Run a comprehension test on a reader with no specialist training. Read the item as that reader would. Score 10 if they would be left with nothing at all, because the pivot is a fact only someone in the field holds, used correctly. Score 8 if they would get that a joke occurred but not what it was. Score 6 if they would get a diminished version of the joke and a specialist would get a sharper one. Score 4 if they would get the same joke, but a specialist would additionally recognize the terminology as apt. Score 2 if the technical words are pure costume and nothing depends on them. Score 0 if there is no technical or specialist material in the item at all. Then apply one check: if the invoked fact is wrong in a way that would stop a specialist from resolving the punch, reduce the score by 3, floored at 0. Score the load the fact carries, not the difficulty of the field.
variants.rationale: Turns a single hinge test into a graded comprehension gap and gives the very common half-accessible case a defined middle score, while the accuracy penalty is made a graded deduction rather than an all-or-nothing disqualification that previously forced items to 0.

variants.name: Platform self-awareness
variants.instruction: Score how far commentary on posting, reading, reposting, forum behaviour, or the act of circulating jokes is part of the joke's own mechanism. 10 = the mechanism is the platform behaviour; remove the posting or reposting frame and the joke does not exist. 8 = platform behaviour supplies the turn, though the same turn could be recast in another medium with some loss. 6 = the item is about the experience of reading or telling jokes and that framing drives the payoff. 4 = the item is set in a posting or commenting situation which supplies the scene while the joke's mechanism is general. 2 = platform language such as posting, feed, comments or upvotes appears as generic decoration. 0 = the text contains no platform, posting, or joke-circulation material at all. Do not score 0 merely because the platform material is decorative; decoration is 2 and absence is 0. Judge only what is written in the text, never anything about who posted it or when.
variants.rationale: 95.5% sat at 0 because the old rule sent both no-platform-material and decorative-platform-material to the same floor. Separating absence (0) from decoration (2), and adding scene-setting and meta-about-jokes rungs, splits the modal bin.

variants.name: Platform self-awareness
variants.instruction: Grade two factors and average, rounding to the nearest whole number. PRESENCE of platform or circulation material in the text, 0 to 10: 0 = none at all, 3 = one incidental mention of posting, reading, sharing, commenting, or reposting, 6 = the item is situated in that activity, 10 = the item is entirely about it. MECHANICAL ROLE, 0 to 10: 0 = the material is inert decoration, 5 = the material carries part of the setup or supplies the situation the punch needs, 10 = the material is the mechanism, so that the joke ceases to work if it is removed. Average the two. This makes an item with no platform material 0, an item mentioning posting in passing about 2, an item set in commenting culture with a general gag about 4 or 5, and an item whose whole turn is a posting behaviour 9 or 10. Judge the text alone; do not guess at the poster, the date, or the item's history.
variants.rationale: Converts a binary mechanism-or-decoration test into a product of presence and role, which forces graded outputs and gives the incidental-mention population, previously all zeros, a nonzero home.

variants.name: Platform self-awareness
variants.instruction: Apply a transplant test. Imagine the item retold aloud between two people in a room, with every reference to posting, feeds, comments, karma, reposting, or the front page removed or converted to ordinary speech. Score 10 if the joke is destroyed, because its self-awareness about being posted and read was the entire mechanism. Score 8 if it survives as a shadow of itself. Score 6 if it survives but loses a distinct layer of irony. Score 4 if it survives fully and only the setting changes. Score 2 if the removal costs nothing at all but such language was present. Score 0 if there was nothing of the kind to remove. Note explicitly that most items in this corpus have nothing to remove and belong at 0, but items where platform words appear without doing work belong at 2 and items merely set in that world belong at 4; do not sweep those into the floor.
variants.rationale: Gives a concrete damage test whose answer is graded, and states in the instruction where the near-floor populations sit so the judge stops collapsing decorative and setting-level platform material into the absence bin.

variants.name: Relatability of Frustration
variants.instruction: Score how much the item taps a widely shared everyday annoyance or social dynamic that readers feel personally, such as scrolling too long, disappointment in content, petty logic, queues, bad sleep, small domestic friction, or workplace absurdity. Grade two factors and average. BREADTH, 0 to 10: 0 = the premise rests on nothing an ordinary reader has lived through, 3 = a situation known to a specific group only, 6 = a situation most adults have met, 10 = a friction essentially everyone has felt. CENTRALITY, 0 to 10: 0 = the frustration is absent or incidental, 5 = a shared irritation supplies the setting while the laugh comes from a pun or an absurd image, 10 = the recognition of the shared frustration is itself the payoff, so the reader laughs because it is true of them. Average and round. A 10 is a universal irritation whose recognition is the joke; a 0 is an artificial or inaccessible premise with no lived friction in it.
variants.rationale: 77% sat at 0 because breadth and centrality were fused into one question that most items failed. Grading them separately and averaging gives real middle scores to the common case of a familiar situation carrying an unrelated gag.

variants.name: Relatability of Frustration
variants.instruction: Score the item by how strongly a typical adult reader would think that is exactly what it is like. 10 = the item names a frustration or petty social dynamic so widely lived that recognition alone produces the laugh. 8 = a broadly shared annoyance is central to the joke, though a device such as exaggeration carries part of the load. 6 = a shared annoyance is present and clearly recognisable, but the joke's engine is elsewhere. 4 = the situation is ordinary and accessible but carries no particular friction, for example a plain everyday setting used as a stage. 2 = the premise is accessible only to a narrow group, or the everyday element is a single incidental detail. 0 = the premise is artificial, abstract, fantastical, or otherwise inaccessible, with no lived annoyance anywhere in it. Judge the shared-frustration content only, not whether the item is funny, and do not speculate about who wrote it.
variants.rationale: Names the plain-everyday-setting case at 4 and the narrow-group case at 2, two large populations the old binary phrasing had to call artificial or inaccessible and therefore sent to the 0 bin.

variants.name: Relatability of Frustration
variants.instruction: Estimate what share of readers would have personally experienced the situation or feeling the joke rests on, and how irritating it is, then combine. If almost nobody has lived it, score 0 to 1. If a specific hobby, profession, or subculture has lived it, score 2 to 3. If most adults have lived it but it is merely familiar rather than annoying, score 4 to 5. If most adults have lived it and it is a genuine small frustration, score 6 to 7. If nearly everyone has lived it and the joke's payoff is the accuracy of the complaint itself, score 8 to 10. Apply this even when the item is also a pun or an absurdity; the shared-frustration content is scored on its own, and a pun set in a universally annoying situation still earns the middle of the range. Score 0 only when the premise contains no lived human situation at all.
variants.rationale: Reframes the criterion as a two-part estimate (prevalence and irritation) mapped onto explicit bands, and states that puns and absurdities still earn mid-range credit for their situational content, which removes the default that pushed them to 0.
